US.01 — Homestead Act & the Transcontinental Railroad

head: Key vocabulary
What it means
rows: An 1862 law that granted 160 acres of public land to settlers who farmed it for five years — accelerating westward settlement.
The 1869 rail line linking the eastern U.S. to the Pacific, built largely by Chinese and Irish immigrant labor.
The 19th-century belief that the United States was destined to expand across the continent.

blocks.label: Modeled example (one worked note — yours will differ)
blocks.text: A key effect of the Homestead Act and the railroad was the rapid settlement of the Great Plains, shown by the millions of acres claimed after 1862, which mattered because it displaced Native nations from lands guaranteed by treaty.
